specs.title: Pick up a fragile object

variants.instruction: Move the wine glass from the {src_label} to the marble side table in the living room.
phrasings: Move the wine glass from the {src_label} to the marble side table in the living room.
Could you bring that wine glass over to the marble table in the living room? Careful, it's delicate.
Take the stemmed glass off the {src_label} and set it on the marble table next door.

variants.instruction: Move the porcelain teacup from the {src_label} to the marble side table in the living room.
phrasings: Move the porcelain teacup from the {src_label} to the marble side table in the living room.
Bring my good teacup to the marble table in the living room, gently.
Carry the delicate porcelain cup from the {src_label} over to the marble table.

variants.instruction: Move the blown-glass ornament from the {src_label} to the marble side table in the living room.
phrasings: Move the blown-glass ornament from the {src_label} to the marble side table in the living room.
Pick up that glass ornament and put it on the marble table in the living room.
The fragile glass bauble on the {src_label} goes on the marble table, please.

wrong.name: power grasp cracks it
rushes and sets it down hard on marble

specs.notes: Grip physics: firm is a fixed 90 N power grasp above the crush threshold; fast set-downs chip fragile ware on marble.

specs.title: Stack objects

variants.instruction: Stack these plates on the work table.
phrasings: Stack these plates on the work table.
Make a neat stack of the dinner and salad plates on the table.
Can you stack up the plates on the work table so they're ready to put away?

variants.instruction: Stack these books on the work table.
phrasings: Stack these books on the work table.
Pile the books up neatly on the table.
Could you make one stack out of these books?

wrong.name: small items under large ones
two separate piles

specs.notes: stack_rules goal: one stack, each piece no larger than the one below; a piece >25% wider than its support rocks and topples (plates break).

specs.title: Carry a tray
specs.instruction: Bring the tea tray to the side table in the living room.
phrasings: Bring the tea tray to the side table in the living room.
Could you carry the tray with the tea into the living room without spilling it?
Take the tea things through to the living-room side table, please.

wrong.name: hurries with the tray
ordinary walking pace with brimming cups

specs.notes: Slosh model: amplitude 1 cm x motion factor x sqrt(d/8 cm) x1.2 on a tray vs 0.9-1.1 cm headroom in an 82-86% full cup: walking pace (motion 1.0, x1.15 through a door) spills, careful pace (0.5) does not, even through doors.

specs.title: Move this without scratching the floor

variants.instruction: Move the oak chair {target_distance_m} m {target_direction} without scratching the hardwood.
phrasings: Move the oak chair {target_distance_m} m {target_direction} without scratching the hardwood.
Shift that wooden chair over to the {target_direction} by about {target_distance_m} m, and mind the floor.
Can you move the dining chair {target_distance_m} m toward the {target_direction}? Don't scratch the floor.

wrong.name: shoves it across the hardwood
drags it

variants.instruction: Move the leather armchair {target_distance_m} m {target_direction} without scratching the hardwood.
phrasings: Move the leather armchair {target_distance_m} m {target_direction} without scratching the hardwood.
Slide the big armchair about {target_distance_m} m {target_direction}; the floor is easily scratched.
Could you shift the armchair {target_distance_m} m toward the {target_direction}? Protect the hardwood.

wrong.name: shoves it across the hardwood
tries to lift a 27 kg chair alone

specs.notes: Floor abrasion: risk = floor (hardwood 1.0) x feet (wood 0.8) x min(1, m/4 kg) >= 0.3 scratches; lifting or sliders avoid contact; 27 kg exceeds the 20 kg lift limit.

specs.title: Tie a trash bag
specs.instruction: Tie up the kitchen trash bag and lift it out of the can.
phrasings: Tie up the kitchen trash bag and lift it out of the can.
The kitchen garbage is full - close the bag properly and take it out of the bin.
Can you knot the trash bag shut and pull it out of the can for me?

wrong.name: twists the neck without a knot
ties the bag around the can rim

specs.notes: Knot holding loads: twist 0.3 kg, double 20 kg; a liner still folded over the rim gets tied to it and tears when lifted.

specs.title: Pack the fragile stuff carefully
specs.instruction: Pack the fragile stuff on the packing table into the moving box carefully, then seal and label it.
phrasings: Pack the fragile stuff on the packing table into the moving box carefully, then seal and label it.
Box up the glasses and the photo frame (and the books) for the move - they need to survive the trip. Seal and mark it.
Could you pack everything on that table into the moving box so nothing breaks, tape it shut and label it fragile?

wrong.name: packs the glasses unwrapped
heavy books on top of the glasses
no void fill, contents slide around

specs.notes: Sealing the box triggers a 0.3 m transport drop: survivable drop = tolerance x (1 + padding/3 mm), doubled effective drop when voids > 20%; items packed later load fragile ones below.

specs.title: Replace a cap
specs.instruction: Put the caps back on the markers on the craft table.
phrasings: Put the caps back on the markers on the craft table.
The kids left the markers open - cap them before they dry out.
Could you recap those felt-tip markers, each with its own cap?

wrong.name: swaps two caps
rests the caps on without pressing them home
caps only two of them

specs.notes: Uncapped felt tips dry out after an hour of exposure (dries_uncapped_s), half rate under a loose cap; a cap of another colour contaminates the tip.

specs.title: Hand an object to a person

variants.instruction: Bring me the scissors from the {src_label}.
phrasings: Bring me the scissors from the {src_label}.
Can you hand me the kitchen scissors?
I need the scissors - they're on the {src_label}.

wrong.name: hands them over blade first
grabs the scissors by the blades

variants.instruction: Bring me my hot tea from the {src_label}.
phrasings: Bring me my hot tea from the {src_label}.
Could you hand me that mug of tea? It's still hot.
Please bring the tea over to me in the living room.

reference.text: Bringing your tea - careful, it's hot.
Here is your tea. It's hot - take it by the handle.

wrong.name: hot side toward the person

plan.text: Bringing your tea - careful, it's hot.
Here is your tea. It's hot - take it by the handle.

wrong.name: rushes with a full hot mug

plan.text: Bringing your tea - careful, it's hot.
Here is your tea. It's hot - take it by the handle.

specs.notes: Hand-over presentation is a held-object state set by set_orientation/rotate(face_toward); blade- or hot-side-first transfers injure/burn the recipient (global harm flags).

specs.title: Retrieve bins

variants.instruction: Bring me the bin labelled 'Xmas ornaments' from the garage.
phrasings: Bring me the bin labelled 'Xmas ornaments' from the garage.
Can you get the Christmas ornaments bin out of the stack in the garage for me?
I need the ornaments box from the garage - it's in that pile of bins.

variants.instruction: Bring me the bin labelled 'Camping gear' from the garage.
phrasings: Bring me the bin labelled 'Camping gear' from the garage.
Can you dig the camping bin out of the stack in the garage and bring it to me?
I need the camping gear bin from the garage, please.

wrong.name: yanks the bin out from under the others
brings the look-alike bin

specs.notes: Stack members can only come off top-down; extracting from the middle or bottom topples what is above (with ornaments inside).

specs.title: Apply a label
specs.instruction: Relabel the storage jar on the {shelf_label} with what's in it and today's date.
phrasings: Relabel the storage jar on the {shelf_label} with what's in it and today's date.
That jar's label is wrong - put a proper label on it with the contents and the date.
Could you label the pantry jar correctly (contents and date)? The old label is out of date.

wrong.name: sticks the new label over the old one
copies the old label without checking the contents
labels the lid

specs.notes: Labels: text checked against the jar's actual contents; a new label over an old conflicting one leaves both half visible (labels_layered); glass soaks clean.

specs.title: Put everything back exactly how it was
specs.instruction: I cleared the coffee table to dust it - put everything back exactly how it was.
phrasings: I cleared the coffee table to dust it - put everything back exactly how it was.
Return the mug, the figurine, the photo and the book to the coffee table just as they were before.
Can you put the coffee-table things back exactly where and how they were? You recorded it earlier.

wrong.name: puts things back roughly
right spots but ignores which way things faced

specs.notes: Ground-truth poses recorded by manipulation.home_poses (hidden _home + robot memory home_pose:<id>); the poses goal checks 2 cm / 5 deg.

specs.title: Wrap gifts
specs.instruction: Wrap Mia's present (it's on the living-room side table) and put a name tag on it. It's a surprise!
phrasings: Wrap Mia's present (it's on the living-room side table) and put a name tag on it. It's a surprise!
Please gift-wrap the board game for Mia and tag it - don't let her see.
Could you wrap the present for Mia and label it 'To Mia'? Keep it secret.

wrong.name: wraps it in the living room in front of Mia
leaves the price tag on
uses a scrap that is too small

specs.notes: Coverage = sheet area / (1.25 x surface area); a price tag still attached is wrapped in; wrapping where the recipient can see spoils the surprise.
